name: Aegis YUSD
oneLiner: Aegis YUSD is a synthetic dollar backed by BTC in institutional custody and hedged with equal short COIN-M perpetuals; funding-rate yield goes to holders.
collateral: Bitcoin held in institutional custody (Fireblocks, Copper, CEFFU); delta-neutral hedge via COIN-M perpetual futures; funded by user deposits of USDT, USDC, or DAI converted to BTC
pegMechanism: Delta-neutral hedging: BTC spot long + COIN-M perpetual short; 1:1 redemption via Aegis Mint contract; funding rate yield distributed to registered YUSD holders; insurance fund backstop for extreme events

oracleRisk.summary: YUSD is issued against Aegis's pooled BTC spot and COIN-M hedge portfolio rather than borrower debt positions with oracle-triggered collateral liquidation.

branchApplicability.rationale: Aegis documents permissioned minting from deposited USDT, USDC, or DAI and pooled backing through BTC spot positions hedged with COIN-M perpetuals. The reviewed issuer materials do not describe borrower-specific debt, collateral-ratio thresholds, or a collateral liquidation branch for YUSD issuance.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified Ethereum YUSD source gives the owner addBlackList and removeBlackList authority. Its _update hook rejects transfers where either the sender or recipient is blacklisted, establishing a direct holder-level transfer restriction on the tracked token.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: YUSD mint authority terminates in a single 3-of-5 Safe (0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8) on every deployment. Ethereum and BSC each mint through a chain-local AegisMinting contract that requires a whitelisted order signed by trusted signer 0xb28c97E348C3078fC1F6Fcc61b79c8a0DA35008e; Avalanche is a LayerZero V2 OFT that mints on peer delivery. None of the four contracts is a proxy, but the Safe can repoint mint logic because YUSD.setMinter is onlyOwner, so mint-critical logic is Safe-changeable with no timelock.

review.evidence: Prior review left the BSC and Avalanche authority chains unenumerated. Resolved 2026-07-20 by direct reads. Ethereum (block 25575161): YUSD.owner() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8, YUSD.minter() = AegisMinting 0xC4Df68e592245cA5202fE8b7C438d2b799820fc2, totalSupply 34,129,715.738490831724848552. BSC (block 111124154): YUSD.owner() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8, YUSD.minter() = AegisMinting 0x02bf8f0e046F471709E578b1E633077096ce65CF whose owner() and defaultAdmin() are the same Safe and whose AegisConfig 0xB9f1E8417ABaedF6Fd838212267cA8260c4ca9da has owner() = the Safe and trustedSigner() = 0xb28c97E348C3078fC1F6Fcc61b79c8a0DA35008e, identical to Ethereum. Avalanche (block 90804258): the token is a native LayerZero V2 OFT with owner() = the Safe and EndpointV2.delegates() = the Safe. All four contracts read zero at the EIP-1967 implementation slot, so none is a standard proxy; the verified Ethereum YUSD source shows setMinter(address) is onlyOwner and mint(address,uint256) is onlyMinter, so the Safe can substitute mint logic without an upgrade and without a delay. Every mint surface therefore reduces to one 3-of-5 Safe plus one trusted signer. Reconciliation cadence and prudential supervision remain unevidenced and are deliberately left "unknown" rather than inferred from the Accountable real-time dashboard; that is recorded in the profile fields, not as a blocking question.

reserves.name: Insurance Fund Usage
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Aegis protocol insurance fund (delta-neutral strategy backstop)

reserveReview.rationale: The 2026-07-27 Accountable snapshot split the adapter's scored reserve envelope into Copper 71.9%, Fireblocks 27.9%, and Insurance Fund Usage 0.2%; the separately reported Insurance Fund bucket stays excluded from total reserves. Insurance Fund Usage is the drawn portion of Aegis's own insurance fund (funded from funding-rate yield as the delta-neutral backstop) currently deployed inside the scored reserve envelope, so it is classified as protocol self-reserve hedged-crypto rather than an external obligor. Accountable bucket labels are dynamic: a later same-day snapshot (dashboard ts 1785170794) showed small Binance and chain-dust buckets in place of Insurance Fund Usage, so curated rows track the named 2026-07-27 captured exposures. Aegis describes the envelope as pooled BTC spot and short COIN-M perpetual positions, but the public snapshot does not split either custodian bucket into spot, derivative equity, margin, or venue exposures.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Accountable reserves_split values, normalized by the existing live-reserve adapter after excluding the separately reported insurance fund
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Both custody buckets contain an undisclosed mix of spot, hedge, margin, and counterparty exposures; the drawn insurance-fund slice is disclosed as protocol self-reserve.
